quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you must install an ignition interlock device in your vehicle, who pays for the installation and monthly inspections?
questions.explanation: An ignition interlock device (IID) measures alcohol in your breath before your car will start. If you have multiple alcohol-related violations on your record, you must install an IID on any vehicle you drive. You pay for the installation and all monthly maintenance costs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light flashes.
Listen, look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly drive under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always listen and look both ways before crossing railroad tracks. Wait for all signals to clear and make sure no train is coming before you proceed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no oncoming traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: You are in a car accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If you can, move it out of traffic. Call police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop any serious bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where pedestrians are present, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking an over-the-counter medication?

options.text: Read the labels for warnings before driving.
Continue to drive no matter what the label says.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels for warnings before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings. If unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Clear a path for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the bridge or overpass ahead is low. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Do what the other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions when they are directing traffic, even if the traffic light says something different.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, you must signal early, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may get stronger.
The effects of both may get weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may get weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Yield to anyone in the intersection. Protect pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: Passing is prohibited:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel during a traffic stop. Ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress, worry, anger, and other strong emotions can reduce your concentration while driving. If you are emotionally upset, wait before driving.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what is important to do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when you don't see other cars.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when you don't see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. Make signaling a habit, not an option.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Drive slowly on wet or slushy roads.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more space to stop and can skid during sharp turns. Don't use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Don't drive if you are tired.
Check that your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you can't see as well. Take steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe in the dark.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the car straight and slowly release the gas pedal to slow down.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slowly release the gas pedal to slow down.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slowly take your foot off the gas pedal. Don't brake until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and drive to a safe place to stop.
